question: Eshwar starts from Point Y and drives 13 km towards the south. He then takes a left turn, drives 27 km, turns right and drives 51 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 18 km. He takes a left turn, drives 35 km. He then turns left, drives 45 km, turns left and drives 18 km to stop at Point Z. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point Y again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution:
Given:

Eshwar starts from Point Y and drives 13 km towards the south.

He then takes a left turn, drives 27 km, turns right and drives 51 km.

He then takes a left turn and drives 18 km. He takes a left turn, drives 35 km.

He then turns left, drives 45 km, turns left and drives 18 km to stop at Point Z.

Movement of Eshwar is,

Since Eshwar's final position (Point Z) is 47 km South and 0 km East/West of his starting point (Point Y), he needs to travel a distance of 47 km in the North direction to get back to Point Y.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
